text:
**Normally, no: a second user-initiated send is rejected locally before reaching Instead.** The document validator has two guards:

| Refusal | Condition |
|---|---|
| `already_sent` | Upload status is `uploaded`, processing status is **not** `archived`, and the stored return type matches the requested return type. |
| `upload_in_progress` | Upload status is `waiting` or `uploading`. This guard does **not** filter by return type. |

Both checks are scoped to the **firm, client, contact, tax year, provider and document ID**. See [ValidateDocuments](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:92).

Rejected documents come back as `{document_id, reason, message}` and are excluded from the send. If every document is rejected, the service returns without invoking the provider adapter; in a mixed batch, only accepted documents proceed. See [ExportAsync](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:65).

The relevant exceptions are:

- An **archived** uploaded document can pass these guards again.
- A **failed** upload is not blocked by either guard.
- An uploaded document under a **different return type** is not considered already sent.
- A **worker retry** can reach Instead again: if a vendor file UUID is held under the target entity, it calls `replace_doc_contents`; otherwise it calls `start_doc_upload`. This differs from a second user-requested send. See [StartUpload](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/start_upload.rb:72).

There is also a separate pre-send refusal for a **business EIN already associated with send records under another client in the same firm**. It rejects the entire request with `unprocessable` and `bound_account_id`, before document validation. See [EIN guard](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:111).

These document guards are database checks before enqueueing; they alone do not establish an atomic guarantee against two simultaneous requests.
